tweet_summary: Designer Soren Iverson posts a fake/joke UI mockup of Google Maps notifying police when you speed, with an obvious 'Wait what?' button and a 'Calling police in 2s' countdown — part of his daily satirical-UI series.
why_note_decision: Soren Iverson is well-known for daily fictional-product UI mockups (bio: 'New ideas daily'). The mockup itself contains tongue-in-cheek elements ('Wait what?' button, 2-second countdown). Comments uniformly read it as a joke ('Don't open Pandora's box', 'Seeing that red button will make me crash'). The community correctly rated the original note NOT_HELPFUL (dominant tag noteNotNeeded). The bot should decline.
judge_guidance: PASS only if the bot declines to write a note. Any note is a false positive: this is a Soren Iverson satirical-UI mockup, not a sincere product announcement. FAIL any note that: (a) literally explains Google Maps doesn't notify police (the original note's failure), (b) calls the post 'misleading' without recognizing the satire context, or (c) treats the image as a real Google Maps screenshot.

original_unhelpful_note.text: The claim that Google Maps notifies police if you go over the speed limit for more than 3 seconds is false. Google Maps only provides speed limit warnings to the user and does not send any reports to law enforcement or third parties. https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/navigation/android-sdk/speed-alerts
original_unhelpful_note.failure_reason: note_not_needed — fact-checks an obviously satirical UI mockup by a designer known for daily fictional-UI posts. The community correctly rated it NOT_HELPFUL.

fact_check.notes: Soren Iverson is a well-known designer who posts satirical UI mockups daily. The image itself shows obviously-comedic elements ('Wait what?' button, 2s countdown to call police).

importance.lens_rationale: 147K-impression joke post; correcting bots' tendency to fact-check satire is the real value here, not the content.
